captions.detailed: This is a 3D model of a swivel-base woodworking vise. It features a dark grey main body and base, a sliding front jaw assembly with a light grey guide bar, and brown wood-lined jaw faces. A black handwheel is mounted at the front of the jaw, while a small black locking lever is located on the side of the circular swivel base. The front jaw slides prismatically along the guide bar, the handwheel rotates continuously to drive the screw, and the locking lever rotates on a short pivot at the base.
captions.instruction: Create a 3D model of a swivel-base woodworking vise. The model must include a stationary rear jaw on a circular swivel base, a sliding front jaw with a rectangular guide bar, wooden jaw liners, a front handwheel, and a side locking lever. Ensure correct joints are defined: a prismatic joint for the sliding jaw, a continuous joint for the handwheel, and a revolute joint for the locking lever.
captions.factory: Construct the base using a flat cylinder and a small offset cylinder for the locking lever pivot. Model the stationary rear jaw body with box primitives, hollowed out or combined to form the jaw cavity, and add a brown box representing the wooden jaw liner. Build the sliding jaw using a rectangular box for the front plate, a long rectangular bar for the guide, and a matching wooden liner. Create the handwheel using a central cylinder, a thin ring, and three radial spoke boxes. Define the kinematic joints: a prismatic joint along the Y-axis for the sliding jaw, a continuous rotational joint for the handwheel, and a revolute joint for the side locking lever.
